rationale: SLICE for the round-6 forearm (both MG90S tab pilots round, Ø1.7 CAD). It replaces the round-3 slice, whose STL predates the ribs and the cross-rib. Profiles from config/printer.json: stock MK3S printer, 0.20mm QUALITY @MK3, Prusament PETG (spec §6 PETG = filament_type in print_requirements). Its 240 then 250 °C, bed 85 then 90 °C and 30-50 % part fan sit inside the requirements' 230-250 / 80-90 °C and the skill's PETG guidance, so they are not overridden. library/materials.csv and lessons.md are empty: no flow, temperature or xy_size_compensation overrides. Overrides meet print_requirements.json exactly: 5 perimeters, 5 top / 5 bottom layers, 40 % gyroid, 0.2 mm layers; elephant-foot compensation 0.2 pairs with the bed chamfer. Orientation is in the STL (brief): flat, FRONT face on the bed, horn pocket, ribs and cross-rib rising from the top; no supports (mesh_check 0.0 % overhang, no bridges). 16.0 mm tall = 80 layers, on the grid. Seam: aligned (now stated explicitly; it is the profile default). Checked in the G-code: the outline's seam is at the horn end (x ≈ -24), away from the x 15 section. The MG90S window's seam is in its far-end corner (x 72.7, y -6.6), 6.6 mm from the far pilot's 1.45 mm strip on the window's centre line, so neither strip carries a seam. Each pilot has its own seam inside the hole, where the self-tapping M2 cuts. Brim: none (brim_width 0): 2875 mm² on the bed holds a flat 129 × 26 plate, and a brim would leave a lip on the front face. 1 copy on 1 plate = spec §7 quantity 1; sliced 2.55 h against the 4 h limit.
